title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is a stable (Deligne–Mumford) curve X of combinatorial type G in 'modular dimension 1'. Every vertex except one, s0, is a rigid trinion (genus 0, three special points). s0 is either genus 0 with 4 special points or genus 1 with 1 special point. The previous page treats the case of genus 0 and order 4: the s0-component is an I-marked projective line Y with I = Â_{s0}, and T_i (i ∈ I) is the unit tangent circle of Y at the marked point i.

Object computed. SP_X is a product over the edges a ∈ Â of sets T_a. Each T_a is the unit circle of the smoothing parameter of the node a, i.e. the unit circle of T_x ⊗ T_y where x, y are the two branches. SP_X is therefore the torus of 'tangential directions' at X: the fibre over [X] of the real oriented blow-up of the boundary of the compactified moduli space (in modern terms, the Kato–Nakayama / log fibre). Its points are the tangential base points used to build the Teichmüller groupoid by gluing local pieces near the boundary. In general T_a = T_{ã} ∧ T_{ã'}, the contracted product over the two half-edges.

Key local fact (used without proof). At a marked point x of a rigid 3-pointed P^1, the unit tangent circle is canonically U ∧_{±1} (Â_{o(x)} − {x}). Here U is the unit circle, and the two-element set of the other two special points serves as a {±1}-torsor. The reason: the coordinate z with z(x) = 0, sending one other point to 1 and the remaining one to ∞, gives a canonical tangent vector d/dz. Swapping the roles of the two other points changes this vector by −1.

Formula for edges away from s0. If s0 is not a vertex of a, then T_a = U ∧_{±1} ε_a. Here ε_a is the contracted product over the two orientations x̃ of a of the two-sets Â_{o(x̃)} − {x̃}. For a free half-edge x at a trinion, ε is simply Â_{o(x)} − {x}.

Formula for edges at s0. There are three cases:
- (I) a is a free marked half-edge at s0: T_a = T_i.
- (II) a is a loop at s0: T_a = T_i ∧ T_j, the product over the two i ∈ J lying over a.
- (III) a joins s0 to a trinion s ≠ s0: T_a = T_i ∧_{±1} (Â_s − {ā}).

Conclusion. SP_X = ∏_a T_a, and each T_i (i ∈ J = Â_{s0}) occurs exactly once; the two ends of a loop occur together in a single factor. The next page splits off the edges A_1 not touching s0, giving SP_X = (U^{A_1} ∧_{{±1}^{A_1}} ε_{A_1}) × T_J^Y. It then decomposes J = J_I ⊔ J_II ⊔ J_III, with a fixed-point-free involution on J_II.

Purpose. This is an explicit combinatorial description of the boundary 'base-point tori' indexed by the pants-decomposition graph G. It is the input for building the Teichmüller groupoids (the 'Lego' of the Esquisse) out of the dimension-1 pieces M_{0,4} and M_{1,1}.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The canonical identification of the unit tangent circle at a point of a rigid trinion with U ∧_{±1} (two-set of the other points) is used without justification, but it is correct.
Case (III) is the only one where the contracted product is over {±1} rather than over U; the notation is coherent once one notices this.
The genus-1, order-1 case for s0 is not treated on this page.

ideas.what: The fibre over a boundary point of the set of tangential directions (smoothing directions) is a torus ∏ over nodes of T_x ∧_U T_y.
ideas.modern_name: Fibre of the real oriented blow-up / Kato–Nakayama space of the compactified moduli space; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kato–Nakayama (1999); Ihara–Nakamura and Nakamura for moduli of curves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to base points at infinity associated with pants decompositions, without this formula

ideas.what: The unit tangent circle at a marked point of P^1 minus 3 points is canonically U ∧_{±1} (two-set of the other marked points).
ideas.modern_name: Canonical tangential base points on M_{0,3} (e.g. 'from 0 toward 1')

ideas.what: Decomposition of the base-point torus into a part from edges not touching s0 and a part T_J^Y depending on the dimension-1 piece Y. The half-edges J at s0 split into free half-edges, loop pairs (with an involution) and edges to trinions.
ideas.modern_name: Product structure of tangential base points along a boundary stratum (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps / Nakamura–Schneps style Lego)

missed.claim: The page gives an explicit, canonical combinatorial description of the torus of tangential base points over a stable curve whose components are all trinions except one. Each edge factor is written as a contracted product of unit circles twisted by the {±1}-torsors given by the two-sets of the other half-edges at a trinion. This anticipates the later standard treatment of tangential base points at maximal degenerations, but it is only an unpublished, explicit version of what Nakamura and others did.
missed.quote: T_i ∧_{±1} (Â_s − {ā}) dans le cas (III), où ā désigne l'arc d'origine s ≠ s0 porté par a
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the precursor in Grothendieck's own hands of the boundary base-point formalism used in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. It is of historical interest for crediting; mathematically it is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, explicit computation of boundary tangential base-point tori, consistent with and anticipating later work by Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps and Lochak. It contains no result absent from the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: 'T_a = ∐_{A_{±1}} ε_a' should read 'T_a = U ∧_{{±1}} ε_a': U is the unit circle and ∧ is the contracted product, not a coproduct. Similarly, on the next page, 'U^{A_1} ∧_{{±1}^{A_1}} ε_{A_1}'.
In the definition of ε_a, '·' should be read as set difference: Â_{o(x)} − {x} and Â_{o(x̃)} − {x̃}, i.e. the two-set of the other half-edges.

'deux fois [?] pour les i ∈ J correspondant à une des deux [?] d'une boucle' is probably not 'twice'. The intended sense is that each T_i occurs once, the two ends of a loop being grouped in one factor T_i ∧ T_j.
The inserted word above 'des cas' is 'trois' (three cases I, II, III). The margin note at top left reads 'Si s0 n'est pas un sommet de a'.
